name: Qwertytwokeyrightshiftcipher

description_json.name: QwertyTwoKeyRightShiftCipher
description_json.idea: A simple, highly deterministic keyboard-based substitution cipher. Each letter is replaced by the letter located exactly two keys to its right on a standard QWERTY keyboard row. Each row wraps around to its beginning. Case is preserved, and all non-alphabetic characters (digits, spaces, punctuation) remain completely unchanged.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
For each character in the input:
1. If the character is not an alphabetic letter, keep it unchanged.
2. Identify the keyboard row of the letter (ignoring case):
   - Row 1: q, w, e, r, t, y, u, i, o, p
   - Row 2: a, s, d, f, g, h, j, k, l
   - Row 3: z, x, c, v, b, n, m
3. Shift the letter 2 positions to the right within its row, wrapping around to the start of the row if it exceeds the row boundary:
   - Row 1 mapping: q->e, w->r, e->t, r->y, t->u, y->i, u->o, i->p, o->q, p->w
   - Row 2 mapping: a->d, s->f, d->g, f->h, g->j, h->k, j->l, k->a, l->s
   - Row 3 mapping: z->c, x->v, c->b, v->n, b->m, n->z, m->x
4. Preserve the original case of the letter.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
For each character in the input:
1. If the character is not an alphabetic letter, keep it unchanged.
2. Identify the keyboard row of the letter (ignoring case):
   - Row 1: q, w, e, r, t, y, u, i, o, p
   - Row 2: a, s, d, f, g, h, j, k, l
   - Row 3: z, x, c, v, b, n, m
3. Shift the letter 2 positions to the left within its row, wrapping around to the end of the row if it goes below the start:
   - Row 1 inverse mapping: e->q, r->w, t->e, y->r, u->t, i->y, o->u, p->i, q->o, w->p
   - Row 2 inverse mapping: d->a, f->s, g->d, h->f, j->g, k->h, l->j, a->k, s->l
   - Row 3 inverse mapping: c->z, v->x, b->c, n->v, m->b, z->n, x->m
4. Preserve the original case of the letter.
